nodes.description: Owner address of the Owned contract, written from msg.sender in the constructor and used as the authority for the onlyOwner modifier.
Tracks the block number of the previous Play() call and is used by protect_mining to block same-block calls.
Constructor of Owned that sets owner = msg.sender.
Access-control modifier requiring msg.sender == owner before executing the body.
Public view returning address(this).balance; consumed by Gamble.getMaxBet().
Owner-only function that destroys the contract and forwards the balance.
Irreversible selfdestruct that sends the whole contract balance to msg.sender; reachable only through the onlyOwner-gated close().
Constant magic = 5 used both as the bet divisor (getMaxBet) and as the timestamp payout modulus.
View that returns getBalance()/magic, i.e. the maximum accepted bet.
Payable game entry point guarded by protect (tx.origin check) and protect_mining; may refund msg.value + msg.value/magic and updates last_blocknumber.
Modifier requiring tx.origin == msg.sender; relies on tx.origin for authorization.
Modifier requiring block.number != last_blocknumber as a simple anti-mining/one-play-per-block guard.
Payable fallback that forwards every plain call to Play().
Caller-controlled address used as owner, as the privileged caller in access checks and as the payout recipient.
now / block.timestamp used in Play() as 'now % magic' to decide the payout, making the outcome timestamp dependent.
Transaction origin used by the protect modifier for authentication, which is unsafe under phishing/proxy calls.
External value transfer of the payout to the caller inside Play(), executed before last_blocknumber is updated.
Unsigned arithmetic computing the refund amount without SafeMath or overflow guards.

edges.reason: The Owned constructor writes msg.sender into the privileged owner state variable.
onlyOwner compares msg.sender with owner to grant privileged execution.
The onlyOwner modifier gates execution of close(), the only balance-draining path.
close() executes selfdestruct(msg.sender), destroying the contract and pushing all funds to the caller.
msg.sender is the beneficiary of the selfdestruct sweep in close().
The payable fallback forwards all plain calls into Play(), so any value-received callback lands in the gambling logic.
protect wraps Play() and enforces the tx.origin == msg.sender authentication check.
protect_mining wraps Play() and enforces block.number != last_blocknumber.
tx.origin is read inside protect and compared to msg.sender, the classic tx.origin authorization weakness.
msg.sender is compared with tx.origin inside the protect modifier.
Play() branches on now (block.timestamp) via 'now % magic != 0', making the payout miner-influenceable (timestamp dependency).
Whether the payout transfer executes at all is determined by the block.timestamp-dependent condition.
Play() calls getMaxBet() in the require(msg.value <= getMaxBet()) check.
getMaxBet() consumes the inherited getBalance() view.
getMaxBet() divides the balance by the constant magic.
Play() writes block.number into last_blocknumber at the end of its body.
protect_mining reads last_blocknumber to reject a second call in the same block.
Play() evaluates msg.value + msg.value/magic with unchecked uint arithmetic (pre-0.8 overflow semantics).
The unchecked arithmetic result is used directly as the amount of the outgoing transfer.
Play() performs the external transfer to the caller while last_blocknumber is still the stale value, so the external call precedes the state update.

The transfer to msg.sender can invoke the recipient's fallback/callback code, which may re-enter the contract's payable fallback before the state update completes (mitigated in practice by the 2300 gas stipend of transfer).
The Owned constructor initializes the owner state variable.
msg.sender is the destination of the payout transfer inside Play().
